title: Your AI already knew the exam: contamination
cover:
Is it smart…
or did it know the exam?

scenes.text: From 75% to 7.5%… on the same kind of exam. What happened?
It's called contamination: the exam questions leak into the data used to train the model.
It's like a student who's already seen the exam: you can't tell if they understand the subject… or just know the answers.
And it happens more than you think: surveys report up to 45% of test material leaked into training data.
That's why the Konwinski Prize only uses GitHub issues filed after the training cutoff. Impossible to have seen them. The winner: 7.5%.
The lesson: a saturated exam is fixed with a harder one. A contaminated one, only with an exam the model has never seen.
So when you see a spectacular score, ask: could this exam have been in its training data?
Because a high score isn't always intelligence. Sometimes, it's memory.
Save it, and share it with someone who believes every leaderboard.
